extraction.summary: The paper introduces an explicit oracle teacher for Active Feature Acquisition (AFA), using labels and unobserved feature values at training time to rank features under a budget. The text describes Active Feature Acquisition (AFA), a method that learns a policy to decide which features to acquire per instance under a budget. Unlike prior AFA approaches that optimize a self‑constructed utility target, this work explicitly constructs a teacher using labels and unobserved feature values to rank candidates by their impact on downstream predictor error. The OracleImitator method then distills this teacher. The text describes a method for learning a feature‑acquisition policy that uses an explicit oracle teacher to rank candidate features by their impact on downstream prediction error, and then distills this ranking into a deployable policy via soft‑target learning. OracleImitator is an active feature acquisition method that builds an explicit oracle teacher ranking candidates by their effect on downstream predictor error, then distills this ranking into a deployable policy via soft‑target imitation. It matches or outperforms existing AFA methods on multimodal medical diagnosis and the AFABench benchmark, recovering 90% of attainable accuracy gain at under a quarter of the acquisition cost.
